info.name: Discord Daily Attendance & Update Automation API
info.description:
API collection for the Discord Daily Attendance & Update Automation backend.

## Authentication Model
- **Admin Only**: System login and dashboard access is permitted exclusively for administrators.
- **Direct Attendance**: Regular users/students do not log in or register; they submit daily attendance directly via the public web attendance form.

## Auto Token Management
The Admin Login request automatically saves the access token as a collection variable. All authenticated requests use it via the collection-level pre-request script.

item.name: Discord
item.description: Discord bot & guild member sync endpoints (requires ADMIN role).

request.description: Requires admin auth. Returns bot connection state, stored member counts (total / active / departed), the last sync summary, and whether #daily-update ingestion is running. `dailyUpdate.ingestionEnabled` is false when the bot fell back to a login without the Message Content Intent — member sync still works, but no daily updates are being recorded.

exec: // The departure guard trips when a member fetch looks truncated,
// which almost always means the Server Members privileged intent is off.
console.warn('⚠️ Departure guard tripped - check the Server Members intent in the Discord Developer Portal');
// Ingestion off is invisible from outside except here: the dashboard would
// simply show every member as missing their daily update.
console.warn('⚠️ Daily-update ingestion is DISABLED: ' + jsonData.data.dailyUpdate.reason);

request.description: Requires admin auth. Starts a full guild member re-sync and returns immediately with 202 Accepted; the sync itself runs in the background. Returns 409 if a sync is already running, or 503 if the bot is not connected.

item.name: Channel Schedule
item.description:
Admin-managed open/lock schedule for #daily-update (requires ADMIN role).

The times are stored in the database, not in code or .env, and take effect without a restart. Times are HH:mm wall-clock in Asia/Dhaka; the cron expression is derived by the backend and never exposed.

Operational prerequisite: the bot needs "Manage Roles" on the channel to edit the @everyone SendMessages overwrite. Without it every open and lock fails and `scheduler.lastRun.error` says so.

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Returns four things:

- `schedule` - the stored openTime, closeTime, daysOfWeek (0=Sunday..6=Saturday), enabled flag, the fixed `timezone` (Asia/Dhaka, reported but never accepted), and who last changed it.
- `scheduler` - whether THIS process runs the timed jobs (`processEnabled`, from SCHEDULER_ENABLED), whether jobs are registered (`running`), `nextOpenAt` / `nextLockAt` as instants, and `lastRun`.
- `channel` - the configured channel ID and its LIVE open state, read from Discord rather than a stored flag.

Check `scheduler.lastRun.error` first when the channel stops opening: a missing Manage Roles permission surfaces here and nowhere else.

exec: // A scheduler that cannot edit the overwrite has no other symptom
// than a channel that never opens.
console.warn('⚠️ Last scheduler run failed: ' + jsonData.data.scheduler.lastRun.error);

request.description:
Requires admin auth. Partial update - send only what changes. Saving destroys and re-registers the cron jobs and reconciles the channel immediately, so a change that puts the current moment inside the new window opens the channel right away.

daysOfWeek uses 0=Sunday..6=Saturday. A `timezone` field is ignored rather than stored.
Runs the schedule Sunday through Thursday only. Editing weekdays is not passive: if today is excluded and the channel is currently open, the reconcile locks it on save.

Rejected with 400. The close time must be strictly later than the open time on the same Dhaka day.

Note this is checked against the MERGED schedule, not the submitted fields: sending only `closeTime` here still fails against the stored `openTime`. A window crossing midnight would file a 00:30 message under the next day, so its author would read as missing on the day they actually submitted.
Rejected with 400. A schedule that can never fire is a mistake, not a way to pause. Use `{ "enabled": false }` to pause while keeping the times.

Requires admin auth. Forces #daily-update open immediately and posts the opening embed. The stored schedule is untouched, so the next scheduled lock still fires normally.

503 if the bot is not connected; 403 if the bot lacks Manage Roles on the channel.

Requires admin auth. Forces #daily-update locked immediately and posts the closing embed. Only SendMessages is denied - members can still read the channel.

This is also how you close the channel after disabling the schedule: disabling stops the scheduler, it does not lock the channel.

item.name: Attendance (Public)
item.description: The web attendance form's two endpoints. These are the ONLY routes in the API with no auth middleware - students are not `users` rows and have no credential to present. Two things stand in for authentication: the handle must resolve to a member currently in the guild, and the caller must be within its per-IP budget (60/min on verify-user, 5/15min on submit). Set the {{attendanceUsername}} variable to a real synced member's handle before running these.

exec: // These endpoints are public: students have no account to log in with.
// The collection-level pre-request adds an Authorization header to every
// request, so remove it here to prove these work with no credentials.
pm.test('Handle verified as a current member', function () {
// `verified` and `alreadySubmitted` live INSIDE `data`, not at the top
// level as the PID sketches them - sendResponse owns the envelope.

request.description:
Live membership check backing the form's verified badge. The handle is normalized first (trimmed, leading @ stripped, lowercased), so ` @Rakib_Dev ` and `rakib_dev` resolve identically.

Returns 200 with `data.verified` true/false - not 404 - because 'not found' is the routine answer the form has to render either way. `data.alreadySubmitted` reports whether this member already has an attendance row for today's Asia/Dhaka date, which `data.attendanceDate` names.

request.description:
A well-formed handle that no active member holds. Still 200; `data.verified` is false and `data.member` is null.

A member who LEFT the guild gets this same response. That collapse is deliberate - both outcomes block submission anyway, and keeping them indistinguishable means this endpoint cannot be used to confirm that a particular person used to be in the server.

request.description:
A format error is a 400 and a DIFFERENT outcome from 'not a member' (200, verified:false). The form needs to tell them apart to say anything useful.

Rejected: consecutive periods, anything outside [a-z0-9_.], under 2 or over 32 characters, discriminator tags like `#0001`.

ACCEPTED: a leading or trailing `_` or `.` - `itzazad_`, `.rabbil`, `shahriarratul.`. 115 of 2189 live members (5.3%) hold such handles. Never tighten the regex to forbid them.

exec: // These endpoints are public: students have no account to log in with.
// The collection-level pre-request adds an Authorization header to every
// request, so remove it here to prove these work with no credentials.
// Re-run this request to see the duplicate refusal (409).

request.description:
Records today's attendance. Exactly four fields; anything else is stripped.

Validation: `name` >= 3 chars, letters and spaces only (Unicode, so Bengali names pass); `phone` as 01XXXXXXXXX or +8801XXXXXXXXX; `email` well-formed; `discordUsername` per the official Discord standard.

Membership is re-verified here even if verify-user was called first. That endpoint is a UI affordance - nothing forces a client to call it, and a member can leave the guild between the two requests. Golden Rule 3 is enforced on this path, not in the browser.

On success the submitted phone and email are also carried onto the member's directory entry, in the same transaction as the insert.

exec: // These endpoints are public: students have no account to log in with.
// The collection-level pre-request adds an Authorization header to every
// request, so remove it here to prove these work with no credentials.
pm.test('Second submission today refused as a duplicate', function () {

request.description:
Run 'Submit Attendance' first, then this. The message names the Dhaka date already submitted for.

The refusal comes from the (member_id, attendance_date) unique constraint, not from a read-then-write check - a pre-check would let two simultaneous submissions both through (Golden Rule 7). Fire two of these at once and exactly one row will exist; the loser gets this same 409.

The contact-detail update is in the same transaction as the insert, so a duplicate leaves the member's directory entry untouched.

request.description:
Golden Rule 3: a handle absent from the guild can never submit. 404 here rather than the verify endpoint's 200, because this is a genuine failure to act rather than a question being answered.

A departed member gets this identical response.
